Chapter 8: The Stories We Tell Ourselves
You know, loneliness isn’t just about the situations we find ourselves in. It’s also about the stories we tell ourselves—about who we are, and how we fit into the world around us. These inner narratives can be incredibly powerful. They shape how we see ourselves, and even how we see other people.
I want you to imagine someone who’s spent years feeling isolated. For them, a big part of that loneliness actually came from a deep-seated belief: that they were just fundamentally different from everyone else. This story played in their mind over and over, until it started to feel true. It became a kind of self-fulfilling prophecy. But here’s the thing—once they started to question that old story, once they began to see themselves as worthy of connection, everything started to shift. That was the first real step toward breaking the cycle.
Maybe you’ve struggled with similar stories—stories of rejection, or of not being enough. Maybe there was a relationship that didn’t work out, a job that slipped away, or a childhood spent feeling like you were always on the outside looking in. These experiences can leave lasting marks, and sometimes, without even realizing it, we let those old stories cloud the way we approach new connections. It can make it so much harder to trust, to reach out, or to even believe that belonging is possible.
But here’s something amazing—art can actually help us rewrite those stories. When we create something, or even just experience someone else’s art, we give ourselves space to see things differently. Think about a painting that captures a moment of vulnerability, or a song that finally puts your unspoken feelings into words. Works like these offer us new stories—ones that make room for hope and connection.
Little by little, it becomes clear that loneliness isn’t just a feeling. It’s a story—and stories can change. When we start to question our old beliefs and open ourselves up to new possibilities, we get to write a different ending. And maybe, just maybe, that’s where real connection begins.
